clue.text: Girl imitates kangaroo in place down under

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
a kangaroo bounds along, so to imitate one is to spring

explanation.surface: A girl hops about like a kangaroo somewhere in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in Australia's Northern Territory, and Australia is the land colloquially called down under.

clue.text: Chain covering a part of Canada

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: an albert is a watch chain, named after Prince Albert

explanation.surface: A mountain chain spreads over a region of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: An albert is an old-fashioned watch chain worn across a waistcoat; 'covering' places it above A in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of Canada's western provinces.

clue.text: That's incorrectly sited

indicators.note: letters placed incorrectly are out of their right order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a thing has been put in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation i.e. stands for a phrase meaning 'that is', used to introduce a clarification.

clue.text: Something vital removed from packages sent, I allege

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, lying within them

explanation.surface: Someone claims a vital item was taken out of parcels in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable is a necessity, the sense of the noun.

clue.text: Burns, for example, last of porridge in cooking-vessel

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the vessel's word

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word porridge is used

explanation.surface: Robert Burns finishes his porridge in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns is Robert Burns, Scotland's national bard, and porridge fits the Scottish picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is an example of a writer of verse.

clue.text: Early during play, performing no business

parts.note: early in a play is in its first act, written IN ACT I
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: A performer early in a show is idle with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: IN ACT I, with the Roman numeral one, is 'early during play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is idleness, the absence of any activity.

clue.text: Gossip about African republic

parts.note: gab is idle chatter
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Chatter concerning a country in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a republic on Africa's west coast.

clue.text: Quarters Oriental leader put a girl, perhaps, inside?

definitions.text: Quarters Oriental leader put a girl, perhaps, inside?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: south and east are two of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so Oriental gives its opening letter
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An eastern ruler installs a girl in the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E, then O, with RAGLI (the rearranged A GIRL) set inside them; the whole clue also describes a harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's apartments in a Muslim palace, a harem.

clue.text: Braved disturbance in one part of speech

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bravely endured a disturbance in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is a word class, modifying a verb, adjective or another adverb.

clue.text: Live with king near Biblical place here in Israel

indicators.note: near says the next piece comes right after the others

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
ER is the abbreviation for Edward Rex, a king
Sheba is the Biblical kingdom of the queen who visited Solomon

explanation.surface: A traveller lives with a king near a Biblical site in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Beersheba is a city in southern Israel's Negev, the 'here' of the clue.

clue.text: Money prayed for on a daily basis

definitions.text: prayed for on a daily basis
definitions.meaning: the Lord's Prayer asks 'give us this day our daily' loaf

explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money and is the daily food asked for in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: What's passed by pupil makes an impression here

definitions.text: What's passed by pupil makes an impression here

parts.words: What's passed by pupil makes an impression here
parts.note: not a schoolchild handing notes, but light passing through the eye's pupil to form an image

explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, where light entering through the pupil forms an image.

clue.text: Extremely old wise man, going out of style

indicators.note: the wise man's word goes around, outside, the word for style

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
tone is manner or style

explanation.surface: An elderly wise man falling out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the Stone Age is prehistoric, used figuratively of anything very antiquated.

clue.text: A new compact for part of Ireland

parts.note: trim means neat and compact

explanation.surface: A fresh agreement for a region of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' looks like a noun meaning pact but is the adjective trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Inhuman ruler?

parts.note: not a cruel tyrant, but a ruler whose authority is held to be divine rather than human

explanation.definitionFit: A theocrat governs in the name of God, a ruler whose claimed authority is divine.

clue.text: A member of one uses it on course

definitions.text: A member of one uses it on course

parts.words: A member of one uses it on course
parts.note: 'one' is a golfing society with members, and also the stick a golfer swings on the course

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a golfing association and the stick a golfer hits the ball with.

clue.text: Able to include game old actor in part of The Cherry Orchard, perhaps

definitions.text: part of The Cherry Orchard, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for able takes the game's letters inside it

parts.note: fit means able or capable
RU is rugby union
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A capable old actor takes a part in Chekhov's play.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'part' is not a role but a component of the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry orchard is made up of trees bearing fruit, so each one is a part of it.

clue.text: Such useful works could be a hit with user

indicators.note: the letters could be turned into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Popular reference books might prove a hit with a reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri are reference books listing synonyms, plural of thesaurus.

clue.text: In the last resort, why report is secret

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged
a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a report is kept secret when all else fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the last resort' reads as an idiom, but 'resort' is re-sort, rearranging THE LAST into STEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or secretive, done covertly.

clue.text: Continue drinking slowly, holding hot bottle

indicators.note: the drinking phrase holds the letter for hot inside it

parts.note: to sip on is to keep drinking in small mouthfuls
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone keeps slowly drinking from a bottle of something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda siphon is a bottle that forces out carbonated water by gas pressure.

clue.text: Strike outside to stop supply

indicators.note: the word for strike goes outside the next word

parts.note: to cuff is to hit with the hand

explanation.surface: Strikers picket outside to halt deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a supply is to discontinue or halt it.

clue.text: Very much a light period for scientist

parts.note: far means greatly, as in far better
the day is the period of daylight

explanation.surface: A much brighter period for a researcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Faraday was the English scientist who discovered electromagnetic induction.

clue.text: Opponent of war, provided one's bound by treaty

indicators.note: the treaty's word wraps around the other pieces, binding them

parts.note: a pact is a treaty
if means provided that
one is I, and one's is short for one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: A war opponent who is bound by an agreement, assuming one is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacifist opposes war and violence on principle.

clue.text: Composer losing royalty, finally, in foreign cash

indicators.note: the composer's name loses a letter

parts.note: César Franck was a Belgian-French composer
K is the abbreviation for king, a royal

explanation.surface: A composer loses his royalties, ending up with foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' says the K for king is taken from the end of FRANCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland and elsewhere.

clue.text: Supplier of furnace right next to pottery centre

indicators.note: next to puts the letter beside the town, after it

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is the heart of English pottery making

explanation.surface: A fuel supplier for a kiln sits next to a ceramics town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke-on-Trent, in Staffordshire, is the centre of England's pottery industry, known as the Potteries.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker feeds fuel to a furnace or boiler.

clue.text: A singer brought up outside African village

indicators.note: the turned bird's word goes outside the letter A
in a down light, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A singer is raised outside a village in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns LARK into KRAL, which goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed village of huts in southern Africa.

clue.text: Duck and swan taken into launch

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape of O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A duck and a swan are taken aboard a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' looks like a boat, which fits the birds, but it means begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to begin it, the verb sense of launch.

clue.text: Old drink out East, a port for the Japanese

indicators.note: the letter for East is taken out

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone finishes an old drink in the East at a Japanese harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan.

clue.text: Having gained for each worker a certain advantage

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, having gained
per means for each
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A worker on piece rates gets a definite edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand means holding a controlling position or advantage.

clue.text: Review of a certain ploy, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Looking back over a particular tactic, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: In sports broadcasting the replay reviews an incident, often a clever ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: An action replay is a televised re-showing of a piece of play, used for review.
